name: Superpowers
definition: A collection of agent skills that turns discovery, design, implementation planning, small-task execution, and review into an enforced development workflow.
author: Jesse Vincent and contributors
availability: Open source plugin; tested with Claude Code
artifactModel: A dated design document followed by a detailed implementation plan whose steps are intended for skill-driven execution and review.
requiredInputs: Human answers during the normal brainstorming loop
taskGrain: Very small implementation steps, commonly framed as a few minutes each with exact files, commands, and tests.
humanReview: The normal workflow pauses for design approval before planning and expects review during implementation. This non-interactive comparison pre-accepted the brief boundary.
iterationLoop: Skills select the next workflow step, run verification, and return to the plan or reviewer when evidence fails.
coupling: High coupling to a compatible coding agent and its skill/plugin loader; the Markdown design remains portable.
customization: Fork or override skills, project instructions, and plan content. The tested plugin ships its workflow as Markdown skills.
portability: Generated Markdown is portable; orchestration semantics depend on the agent skill runtime.
friction: Low install friction through a plugin directory, but the plan stage stalled twice in this bounded headless run.
caveats: Two bounded plan attempts stopped making progress and were interrupted.
The design selected technical choices that the shared brief left open.

name: GSD
definition: An agent-operated project system that keeps requirements, a phased roadmap, current state, phase context, plans, and verification records in a `.planning` directory.
author: Open GSD and contributors
availability: Open source npm package; tested with Claude Code
artifactModel: A persistent project ledger: project definition, numbered requirements, phased roadmap, resumable state, then phase-specific context and plans.
requiredInputs: Workflow preferences such as phase granularity and verification
taskGrain: Roadmap phases first, then executable plans and tasks within one phase.
humanReview: The workflow exposes decision points at project setup and phase discussion; plan checking and verification add machine review gates.
iterationLoop: `.planning/STATE.md` records position, decisions, blockers, and session continuity so later agent runs resume the roadmap.
coupling: High coupling to installed slash commands and agent helpers; the planning ledger itself is plain Markdown and JSON.
customization: Profiles, phase granularity, parallel planning, model profile, research, planning checks, verification, and source-grounding options.
portability: The ledger is easy to inspect anywhere; executing it as designed needs the GSD command set.
friction: One npm install command plus interactive or scripted setup. The isolated run upgraded from core to full profile to make its roadmap helper available.
caveats: Project, requirements, roadmap, state, and phase context completed.
The first phase plan did not complete in the bounded run.
The workflow modified and committed files inside its isolated run repository.

name: GitHub Spec Kit
definition: A spec-driven development toolkit that turns a project constitution and feature statement into a specification, implementation plan, supporting design artifacts, and ordered tasks.
author: GitHub
availability: Open source Python CLI with integrations for multiple coding agents
artifactModel: A repository constitution plus one feature directory containing the spec, requirements checklist, plan, research, data model, contracts, quickstart, and tasks.
requiredInputs: A feature statement focused on user need
Repository and technology context for planning
taskGrain: Ordered implementation tasks grouped by setup, foundations, and independently testable user stories.
humanReview: Constitution, specification clarification, plan decisions, and the generated task list are explicit inspection seams before implementation.
iterationLoop: Each command reads the prior artifacts; constitution checks and feature checklists surface conflicts before later stages.
coupling: Medium coupling: the CLI installs commands for a chosen agent, while its artifacts and shell scripts are repository files.
customization: Project constitution, templates, extension hooks, agent integration, and feature-specific decisions.
portability: High artifact portability across supported agents and normal Git tooling.
friction: Requires the Python CLI and an initialization step. It produced the largest complete artifact tree in this run.
caveats: The source checkout reports a development version rather than a release tag.
The plan made several technical decisions absent from the brief.

name: Kiro Specs
definition: Kiro's feature-planning workflow that develops requirements, a technical design, and an implementation task list as three linked documents.
author: Kiro
availability: CLI download available; authenticated Kiro session required for the workflow
artifactModel: Three linked files: EARS-style requirements, technical design, and requirement-traced implementation tasks.
requiredInputs: Human feedback while requirements and design evolve
taskGrain: Numbered implementation tasks and subtasks tied back to requirement identifiers.
humanReview: Each of the three documents is a natural approval seam; the documented workflow encourages iterative refinement before execution.
iterationLoop: Conversation updates requirements, design, or tasks; downstream documents remain linked to earlier decisions.
coupling: High coupling to the Kiro product for generation and task execution; the three Markdown artifacts remain readable elsewhere.
customization: Project steering and conversational refinement shape generation; no reusable vendor templates are copied here.
portability: Markdown artifacts are portable, while the documented generation and execution loop is a Kiro feature.
friction: The CLI installer and browser authentication add vendor setup. That authentication was unavailable to this run.
caveats: No Kiro tool generated these files.
The original example follows public documentation and is labeled manual on every file.
No proprietary template content is included.

name: Matt Pocock's skills
definition: A set of coding-agent skills that turns a feature conversation into a durable specification, then converts the approved spec into tracker-ready tickets.
author: Matt Pocock and contributors
availability: Open source agent plugin; tested with Claude Code
artifactModel: A published implementation-ready spec followed by a reviewed breakdown into issues for a configured local or remote tracker.
requiredInputs: A feature request and repository context
Human review of the spec and proposed ticket breakdown in normal use
taskGrain: Tracker-sized tickets with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and enough context for a coding agent.
humanReview: The spec is reviewed before publication; the skill then asks for approval of the ticket breakdown before creating issues.
iterationLoop: Revise the durable spec, regenerate or edit the proposed ticket set, then work ticket by ticket.
outputFiles: One issue or local Markdown file per approved ticket
coupling: High coupling to the agent skill runtime and configured issue tracker; written specs and local tickets are portable.
customization: Tracker choice, labels, domain-document layout, project instructions, and the spec/ticket review flow.
portability: Local Markdown mode is portable; remote tracker integrations tie execution to that service.
friction: Requires plugin setup and tracker configuration. The comparison uses local Markdown so it cannot change external systems.
caveats: The setup command stalled without writing files, so the spec skill was invoked directly.
The run produced one spec and 11 local Markdown tickets.
The comparison pre-approved the local ticket breakdown to keep the run non-interactive; normal use includes a human approval seam.

name: BMad Method
definition: A modular, agent-oriented development method with separate workflows for briefs, requirements, architecture, epics, stories, implementation, review, and a faster technical-spec path.
author: BMad Code, LLC and contributors
availability: Open source npm installer with integrations for coding agents
artifactModel: A broad library of role and workflow artifacts; the tested express path emits one technical spec plus a memory log before quick development.
workflow: Choose full planning or express spec path
taskGrain: Ranges from epics and stories in the full method to capabilities and implementation slices in the express technical spec.
humanReview: Full workflows expose product, architecture, readiness, story, and review gates. The headless spec path replaces live questions with explicit assumptions and open questions.
iterationLoop: Workflow-specific validation and correction skills feed changes back into the current artifact; the memory log preserves headless progress.
outputFiles: Additional PRD, architecture, epic, story, and review files in the full path
coupling: High coupling to installed BMad skills and agents during generation; emitted Markdown remains inspectable and portable.
customization: Modules, agent host, output language and path, user skill level, per-skill customization files, and full versus express workflow.
portability: Artifacts are plain files, but reproducing the staged method requires the installed BMad bundle.
friction: The installer adds a large workflow and skill tree. The express spec command itself produced a compact result without interaction.
caveats: Only the express technical-spec path was run, not the full PRD/architecture/epics path.
The output includes 12 unresolved questions rather than silently choosing every technology.
The installed framework tree is not copied into this repository.
